criteria.text: Cardiomyopathy of wild type or hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR-CM), the closed FDA-labeled indication.
Patient is 18 years of age or older (approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a cardiologist (approval criterion 2).
ATTR-mediated amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy confirmed by cardiac biopsy amyloid deposits OR confirmation of a TTR mutation by genetic testing or wild type amyloidosis (approval criterion 3).
Clinical symptoms of cardiomyopathy and heart failure are present (approval criterion 4).
Patient has not had a liver or heart transplant (approval criterion 5).
Patient does not have NYHA class IV heart failure (denial criterion 6).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Vyndaqel (tafamidis meglumine) / Vyndamax (tafamidis), transthyretin (TTR) stabilizers. Version 1; Original 8/13/2019; Approval 11/15/2019; Effective 1/6/2020.
Encoded: closed ATTR cardiomyopathy indication, approval criteria 1-5 and denial criterion 6 (NYHA class IV). Denial criteria 1-5 mirror approval requirements.

Cautions (notes only): tafamidis may cause fetal harm; contraception is recommended for females. Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment due to potential serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant.
Vyndaqel and Vyndamax are not equivalent on a per mg to mg basis (notes only).
Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization approval up to 12 months. No additional reauthorization response criteria are stated.

Quantity limits (notes only): Vyndaqel 120 capsules of 20 mg (80 mg per day); Vyndamax 30 capsules of 61 mg. The PDF does not specify a quantity-limit time interval. max_units is null; quantity is not evaluated.
Documentation verification, cautions, duration, reauthorization and quantity limits require manual review; this pack remains partial. No alternatives are specified.
